entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Muḥammad ibn Hibbān al-Bustī (unknown–965 CE) was a pivotal figure in the development of Shafi'i traditionist and ḥadith criticism, significantly influencing Islamic scholarship and the preservation of Islamic knowledge.








 Al-Bustī's prodigious writings spanned multiple disciplines, including fiqh, astronomy, medicine, and history, cementing his reputation as a polymath and polymathic scholar.








 His critiques of ḥadith and rijal, in particular, continue to shape the field of Islamic scholarship to this day, with his work remaining a primary source for many ḥadith scholars and historians.








 Despite the passing of centuries, Ibn Hibbān's contributions to Islamic scholarship remain an integral part of our understanding of Islamic history and culture.
